name: Yugoslavism
summary: Yugoslavism holds that the South Slavs, above all Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, are one people by blood, language and interest and should be united politically. It grew out of the Illyrian movement and was pursued in the Corfu pact of 1917, the interwar kingdom and, in a socialist form, Tito's brotherhood and unity. Its strands disagreed mainly over whether the nation should be merged into one centralised nation (integral) or be a federation of historical lands.
scope: The profile represents the mainstream of political Yugoslavism between the Illyrian movement and the interwar kingdom, based on the 1917 Pact of Corfu and on integral Yugoslavism (Antić and Dragosavljević on ORJUNA). Federalist and socialist (Titoist brotherhood and unity) strands are noted but where they diverge, especially on economics, the answer is neutral and low-confidence. Excludes later Yugonostalgia and Serbian or Croatian nationalism as such.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Yugoslavism was a national-unity idea with no health programme; its adherents ranged from liberals to Communists, whose federation later provided state health care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No wage policy belongs to the idea of South Slav unity; supporters of Yugoslavia split along ordinary left-right lines.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine is silent on economic systems and was held by bourgeois nationalists and Titoist socialists alike, so the answer is genuinely split.

public-ownership.rationale: Interwar Yugoslavists were mostly liberal or monarchist while socialist Yugoslavism ran state and social ownership, so no single position defines the ideology.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation never featured in the Yugoslav national idea; adherents divided by party and era.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed; integral Yugoslavists such as ORJUNA fought left-wing labour while socialist Yugoslavists backed unions under the party.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Corfu pact promised equality before the law but no property doctrine, and socialist Yugoslavists later nationalised property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No position in the core idea; left to the economic views of each adherent.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not part of the ideology, and its adherents spanned the full economic spectrum.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only the socialist strand, with its self-management, would agree; the interwar monarchist mainstream would not, so the ideology itself is split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Integral Yugoslavists of the interwar state used coercion freely, but the idea has no stated line on surveillance; inferred split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by a 19th and early 20th century national-unity movement.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Brotherhood and Unity led to convictions for nationalist agitation, which suggests the socialist strand would agree, but the interwar strand is unclear.

strong-leader.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism backed King Alexander's 1929 personal rule, while the Corfu strand wanted a parliamentary monarchy, so adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: Yugoslavism aimed at building a state, the Corfu pact specifying a constitutional kingdom with unified power, so the claim that the state is harmful is alien to it.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is outside what Yugoslavists wrote on; nothing in the unity programme implies a side.

empower-police-military.rationale: Integral Yugoslavists relied on the army, police and ORJUNA squads to enforce unity, but the idea has no budget position, so this is inferred only.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A moral-legal question that Yugoslav nationalists never took up, and adherents of different faiths would differ.

decide-locally.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism favoured centralisation to merge peoples into one nation, though federalist Yugoslavists wanted regional autonomy, so the mainstream leans against localism.

rehabilitation.rationale: Yugoslavist sources discuss nation and state, not penal philosophy, so no position can be shown.

traditional-family.rationale: No family doctrine in the core idea; conservative monarchists and secular socialists both held it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the traditional, mostly early 20th century milieu of its mainstream.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between Catholic, Orthodox, Muslim and secular backgrounds.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Corfu pact insisted on equal religions and religious harmony, and ORJUNA attacked clericalism of both churches as a divider of the one nation.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; no race framework in the doctrine.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The doctrine contains no theory of gender; religious and secular adherents would differ.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Yugoslavists defended South Slav language and culture against Germanisation and Magyarisation from the Illyrian movement on, though the nation they meant was the Yugoslav one.

gradual-change.rationale: Young Yugoslav nationalists were radicalised revolutionaries, and the state-building of 1918 was a sharp break, though the Corfu strand was more legalist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; the idea concerned the unity of peoples already in the region.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; later Yugoslavia led the Non-Aligned Movement but that is not part of the core idea.

free-trade.rationale: No trade doctrine in the idea; its adherents' views varied.

nation-first.rationale: A nationalism for the Yugoslav nation, so it places that state's interests first, but it does not set itself against cooperation as such; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Yugoslavist writings do not discuss foreign interventions for human rights; the idea is about unifying one region.

open-borders.rationale: Yugoslavism sought a single bordered state for the South Slavs and nothing in it suggests open borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits on growth were not a concern of a 19th and early 20th century unity movement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for the doctrine, so left neutral.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Yugoslavism has no theory of technology and progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power postdates the movement's formative debates and socialist Yugoslavia's later reactor plans were not part of the idea.

revolution-justified.rationale: Young Yugoslav nationalists in the Habsburg lands used conspiracy and violence against the empire, and unity itself required overthrowing it.

experts-over-public.rationale: The doctrine does not discuss technocracy versus popular rule beyond calling for elections in the Corfu pact.

central-planning.rationale: Only the early socialist strand planned centrally, and it was later decentralised; the core idea has no economic system.

socialized-markets.rationale: Only the Titoist strand's self-management matches this; the rest of the ideology has no view.

land-value-tax.rationale: Fiscal theory of land taxation never entered Yugoslav nationalist programmes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxes were not part of the unity programme and economic views divided adherents.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional income is a modern proposal unrelated to the Yugoslav national idea.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The doctrine has no trade policy; economic nationalism and liberalism both appear among adherents.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Socialist Yugoslavia did this, the interwar kingdom less so, so adherents split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed; peasant-based Yugoslavist parties would agree, socialists would not.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Even socialist Yugoslavia kept money and wages, and the interwar mainstream was non-socialist; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions were not debated in Yugoslavist texts.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a stated Yugoslavist position, though some integral nationalists of the 1920s-30s flirted with corporatist ideas; split.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Corfu pact promised a democratic parliamentary system, but the socialist strand ran a single party, so this is a lean only.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Corfu envisaged a constitutional monarchy under the Karadjordjevic dynasty, and the interwar kingdom was its main vehicle, though the socialist strand was republican.

democracy-best.rationale: The Corfu pact specified a democratic parliamentary monarchy with universal, equal, direct, secret suffrage, but interwar integralists overrode parliament.

direct-votes.rationale: The pact called for elected representation and a constituent assembly, not referendums; no stated view.

workers-councils.rationale: Socialist Yugoslavism used workers' councils in self-management but political power rested with the party; the wider ideology did not.

right-to-secede.rationale: Yugoslavists held that the South Slavs are one nation, and the interwar state and its ideology treated separatism as illegitimate; the Corfu pact barred detaching territory without consent of the nation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Yugoslavism claims no natural-rulers theory; the Corfu pact relied on dynasty and elections instead, so adherents leave it open.

political-violence-never.rationale: Yugoslav nationalists before 1914 and ORJUNA in the 1920s openly practised and praised political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: ORJUNA cultivated a cult of struggle, but this was not a mainstream tenet of the wider idea.

separate-church-state.rationale: The pact required equal rights for Orthodox, Catholic and Muslim faiths and state-protected religious harmony, which is neither strict separation nor an established church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Corfu pact placed three religions on an equal footing under common law, which rules out religious law as the basis.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Yugoslavism was about building a unified state with unified power, so privatised state functions are alien to it; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Not a doctrine; integral Yugoslavists were expansionist toward neighbours but a rival-focused arms stance is not stated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Corfu pact calls Serbs, Croats and Slovenes one nation united by blood and language, and the theory held that the South Slavs form a single ethnic nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Interwar Yugoslavism, which was nationalist, put nation above class, but socialist Yugoslavism accepted Marxist history; lean against.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Outcome equality is an economic question the nationalist strand ignored and the socialist strand pursued only partly.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims have no analogue in the doctrine, which is about merging South Slav peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Yugoslavism was anti-Habsburg, not concerned with overseas colonialism, and gives no view on reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Yugoslavism united peoples across Orthodox, Catholic and Muslim faiths, so it joins by kinship of language, not shared religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Yugoslavism has no ethical theory about self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Integral Yugoslavists subordinated particular national identity and party to the national state, but they did not state a doctrine of duties versus rights; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy was not part of the Yugoslav idea.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy was never a theme of Yugoslavist writing.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; progress-minded modernising nationalists would not agree.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The idea says nothing about the pace of technological disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist ideas are anachronistic for a nationalism of this era.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Algorithmic governance is anachronistic for Yugoslavism.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is anachronistic for the doctrine.

restore-past-order.rationale: Yugoslavists aimed at a new nation and state, though some pseudo-historical claims invoked a lost shared Slavic past.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Yugoslavists were committed to an ideological national project, but the idea does not say how to judge policy.

direct-action.rationale: Pre-1914 radical Yugoslavists and ORJUNA used direct action, while Corfu-style moderates used parliaments; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: The doctrine has no principle linking methods to the final society, and its adherents used both violence and parliaments.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly outside the doctrine of a modern state-building nationalism; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Only utopian communism proposes this, and Yugoslavism does not.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist aim stated in socialist Yugoslavia but not part of the wider idea.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist Yugoslavism would agree, the liberal-monarchist mainstream would not.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist Yugoslavists would agree and nationalist ones would not.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Corfu strand promised a democratic parliamentary state; only the Communist strand sought class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Briefly tried in socialist Yugoslavia and abandoned; the interwar idea was not collectivist.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Only the Marxist strand might say this, and the core unity idea takes no view on the causes of war.

taxation-theft.rationale: A statebuilding creed with a unified state has no objection to taxation; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal limits on state power are not a Yugoslavist theme, and the interwar state curbed speech for unity.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Corfu pact recognised equal rights of citizens but also named collective nations, flags, religions and alphabets as bearers of rights.

conscription.rationale: The interwar Yugoslav state built a conscript army and the idea of a Yugoslav armed nation was prominent in ORJUNA; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The Corfu pact stressed universal suffrage and a constituent assembly as the means of consent.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers has no counterpart in a state-building nationalism.

positive-liberty.rationale: The distinction between negative and positive liberty is not discussed in Yugoslavist sources.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claims of media and university dominance are not part of the doctrine.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Yugoslavists spoke of one South Slav race or blood, but without a doctrine of group ability differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Some integral nationalists favoured corporatist ideas but the Corfu strand called for universal suffrage.

total-state.rationale: The interwar state was centralised and coercive but not totalitarian in doctrine; lean against.

national-rebirth.rationale: Yugoslav nationalists presented a new united nation as a break from fragmentation and foreign rule, not an answer to decadence; weak inference.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Integral Yugoslavists made claims on neighbouring lands, such as Carinthia and Macedonia, but expansion was not a general doctrine of the mainstream.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contradicts the constitutional, parliamentary state the Corfu pact specified.

bound-labor.rationale: Contradicts the equality of all citizens before the law in the Corfu pact.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology of power is outside the idea, although pseudo-historical claims shaped it.

universal-morality.rationale: Yugoslavism has no moral philosophy of its own.

single-common-good.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism asserted a single national interest above party and region, but the doctrine was not framed as philosophy.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Yugoslavism takes no position on Zionism, and Yugoslav policy toward Israel changed over time.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Yugoslavists do not set out a right of return for emigrants, although Yugoslav emigres fed the Yugoslav Committee.

revive-national-language.rationale: Yugoslavists did promote a common Shtokavian literary standard, but that was not reviving a lost language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Titoist strand's self-management is relevant; other adherents had no view.

school-vouchers.rationale: School choice funding is a modern policy debate absent from the doctrine.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not part of the idea.

economic-freedom.rationale: Yugoslavism does not link political and economic freedom; liberal and socialist adherents would answer oppositely.

rule-by-example.rationale: The pact prescribed constitutional law and elections.

national-self-determination.rationale: Yugoslavists claimed self-determination for the single South Slav nation against Habsburg rule, but denied it to Serbs, Croats and Slovenes separately.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN did not exist when the idea formed, and socialist Yugoslavia valued the UN as a Non-Aligned state but that is not core.

reason-over-faith.rationale: ORJUNA was anticlerical, but the doctrine does not take a stance on reason versus faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants was not an issue the doctrine addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not part of the doctrine.

class-collaboration.rationale: The nationalist strand placed the nation above class division, so cooperation is the lean; the Marxist strand differs.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Contradicts the idea's emphasis on shared South Slav heritage; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Socialist Yugoslavia led the Non-Aligned Movement but that is not core to Yugoslavism.

workers-nation.rationale: The ideology's own stress on a unified nation over class-based or particularist lines; socialist strand favoured internationalism too.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender roles in law were not specified by the idea; socialist Yugoslavia formally equalised them but the earlier mainstream did not.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a non-Islamic-economics modernising movement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equality of all citizens before the law was a Corfu commitment, and Yugoslavism rests on uniting peoples.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist Yugoslavists accepted it and nationalists did not.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production policy is not part of Yugoslavism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Integral Yugoslavists pressed minorities and the South Slav peoples themselves to merge into one nation; applied to immigrants by inference.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; a conspiracy theory outside the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: The pact required equal, direct, secret suffrage but did not specify the electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed beyond spreading Yugoslav unity itself.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The structural analysis of patriarchy is not part of the doctrine.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not a Yugoslavist doctrine; nationalists criticised Habsburg and later rival parties rather than elites as such.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics was not a Yugoslavist programme, though 'blood' language appeared in the unity claim.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; the socialist state prosecuted opponents but not its own security forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Yugoslavism sought a strong unitary or federal state, and the interwar and socialist states were interventionist; lean against.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: A movement to merge Serbs, Croats and Slovenes into one people opposes discouraging mixing across groups.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Corfu pact declared all citizens equal in rights before the state and law.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Only the socialist strand matters here, and Titoist Yugoslavia broke with the Soviet line.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No Yugoslavist discussion of settler colonialism exists.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Corfu pact called for equality before the law with unified power, but also separate religious communities; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The pact guaranteed free practice of all religions.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-cultural issue irrelevant to South Slav unity, where Muslims, Christians and secular citizens coexist.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious equality was guaranteed but schooling policy is not stated.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The pact provided for a constituent assembly elected by universal suffrage and consent of the nation, though the interwar state ignored that.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export surpluses were not discussed in the doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: ORJUNA terrorised minorities but the doctrine did not propose transfers; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Yugoslav nationalists used and justified force for unification and ORJUNA fought minorities and opponents, so absolute non-aggression is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: ORJUNA had a cult of struggle but it is not general doctrine.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The interwar kingdom banned the Communist Party in 1921 and later separatist parties; inferred as the practice.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not found in Yugoslavist sources.

separated-powers.rationale: The pact called for a parliamentary constitutional monarchy, implying checks, but interwar centralism undermined them.

vanguard-party.rationale: Only the Communist strand held a vanguard theory, and the national idea itself does not.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Care for the poor is not a distinguishing theme of the national idea, though socialist Yugoslavia stressed workers.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy question with no connection to Yugoslavism.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Integral Yugoslavists attacked left labour militancy, but no stated stance on strike law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian explanations of poverty play no part in the doctrine.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Integral Yugoslavists held that separate Serb, Croat and Slovene identities weakened the state, but the claim concerns subnational identities rather than diversity generally.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contradicts the elected parliament in the Corfu pact.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: King Alexander suspended the constitution in 1929 in the name of unity, and the state used coercion; but the Corfu strand opposed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls were used by both interwar and socialist states but not as a tenet of the idea.

party-controls-media.rationale: Socialist Yugoslavism controlled media through the party and the monarchy censored, but the Corfu strand did not state this.

party-commands-army.rationale: Only the Communist strand put the army under party command, and interwar Yugoslavism put it under the king.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods were not a concern of the idea.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: MP pay was not a Yugoslavist topic.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is not addressed by the idea; the Communist strand had it and the monarchist strand did not.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Yugoslavism itself merged several peoples into one state, but the statement is about supranational unions; weak inference.

head-commands-forces.rationale: King Alexander commanded forces in the interwar state, but the Corfu text spoke of parliamentary government.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not addressed; the idea spanned Orthodox bishops, Catholic bishops and the Islamic community.

clerical-rule.rationale: Contrary to the pact's equal treatment of three religions under a civil state and ORJUNA's anticlericalism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Leninist position outside the national idea.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship is not a theme of the doctrine, though integral regimes did censor.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term limits are not discussed for a monarchy-minded or later party-led movement.

recall-officials.rationale: The recall of elected officials is not part of the doctrine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The Little Entente alliances of the interwar kingdom and later Non-Alignment pull in different directions.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Home ownership as a right is a distinct programme that Yugoslavism never advanced.

people-in-arms.rationale: The ORJUNA ideal of armed nationalists and the later Territorial Defence of socialist Yugoslavia point toward it, but the mainstream kept a standing army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; peasant parties and Yugoslavism overlapped but it is not core.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Corfu pact claimed all lands compactly inhabited by the nation, and Yugoslavism sought to unite South Slavs divided among Habsburg lands, Serbia and others.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was intellectual in origin.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The pact gave Serb, Croat and Slovene names, alphabets and faiths equal standing, though this is about a single nation's components.

death-penalty.rationale: Executions for the gravest crimes were not a point of Yugoslavist doctrine, and both the interwar and socialist states used them.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curricula on sex education are not part of the doctrine; religious and secular adherents differ.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: ORJUNA denounced religious fanaticism and clericalism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Corfu pact defined the nation by blood and language, which suggests descent; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Corfu equalised alphabets and names for the three South Slav peoples, but integral Yugoslavists and ORJUNA attacked minority-language media of non-Slavs.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Corfu pact assured freedom of religion but not exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument about social conformity is not part of Yugoslavism, which pressed for national conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt politics came later than the idea, though socialist Yugoslavia joined Non-Aligned demands.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Only the socialist strand framed it this way.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Corfu pact explicitly provided that the constitution be drafted by a constituent assembly elected after the war.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Both King Alexander's dictatorship and the Communist state restricted freedoms, but not as a stated development doctrine.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are not part of the doctrine.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the idea's formation; socialist Yugoslavia explored but did not build them.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The pact specified a hereditary king, not an elected head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank independence was not discussed in Yugoslavist sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The pact barred ceding any part of the nation's territory without the nation's consent, so Yugoslavists oppose giving up lands for peace.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The doctrine has no property theory; socialist adherents would agree and liberals would not.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; the Tito-Stalin split led Titoists to critique Soviet bureaucracy but not necessarily as state capitalism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrine is absent from the idea.

collective-defense.rationale: The interwar kingdom had defensive alliances, but no stated doctrine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Yugoslavists contested Habsburg rule over South Slav lands, but the doctrine does not state a general rule on annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: ORJUNA wanted the churches checked as divisive, but the interwar regime favoured the Serbian Orthodox Church, so this is split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Corfu pact's constitutional monarch under the dynasty fits a unifying symbol, but interwar kings governed directly.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The interwar Yugoslav state and ORJUNA treated Croat and Slovene separatism as treason to be suppressed, and the socialist state likewise prosecuted separatists.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The pact promised local autonomies on natural, social and economic lines, yet the integral mainstream rejected special regimes.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Corfu pact specified a constitutional, parliamentary monarchy, not a sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax rate structures were not part of Yugoslavism.

character-from-environment.rationale: Yugoslavists called the nation one by blood and language but had no stated theory of upbringing versus nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The pact required a constitution and parliament, though King Alexander ruled by decree after 1929.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is anachronistic for the doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The pact's constitutional monarchy with parliament is mixed, but the doctrine is not framed so.

leader-cult.rationale: Tito's cult in socialist Yugoslavia and the royal cult interwar fit, but it is not a stated tenet.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules are outside the idea.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Titoism did not state this and Yugoslavism as a whole does not address it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Interwar Yugoslavia did carry out agrarian reform, but it is not a doctrine of the idea.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not a theme of the doctrine, which concerned unity before the wars of the 1990s.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Corfu pact claimed all lands compactly inhabited by the one nation, and integral Yugoslavists pushed claims on neighbours' South Slav populations such as Carinthia and Macedonia.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Corfu pact required free and public exercise of recognised religions.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contrary to the modernising, secular-leaning mainstream; weak inference.

common-currency.rationale: Yugoslavism supported a single state and so a single currency, but the question is about multi-country currencies; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: This is the core of Yugoslavism: that the South Slavs, sharing language and ancestry, belong in one state or nation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The pact gave equal national names and flags to Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, but integral Yugoslavists wanted them merged, so the ideology is split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Diaspora strategy is not part of Yugoslavism; its relevant minorities were Slavs inside or beside the future state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Marxist strand would agree and the nationalist strand would not.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust and economic concentration were not a theme of the doctrine.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts did not feature in Yugoslavist thought.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional courts versus majorities is not covered by Yugoslavist sources.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not part of the doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Imperial autarky blocs are not a Yugoslavist idea.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements and linked standards are not part of the doctrine.

moral-incentives.rationale: Only the socialist strand used such rhetoric.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Young Bosnia and similar groups acted on this idea in the Habsburg lands, but it is not a doctrine of the mainstream.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: ORJUNA criticised feudalism, yet the interwar mainstream backed a hereditary monarchy.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Yugoslavism had no overseas colonial project, and nothing implies civilising tutelage.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-conscious admissions are not part of the doctrine.

patriotic-education.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism worked to inculcate a single Yugoslav national identity through schools and state symbols, notably teaching one language and nation.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary theory is absent from the idea.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Marxist crisis theory debate is outside the national idea.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Yugoslavists sought freedom from the Habsburg empire, and the doctrine does not call for cultivating influence in former empire lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory proposals do not belong to Yugoslavism.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis foreign to the national idea.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The pact called for equal rights before the law for all citizens.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The pact required a constitution needing a qualified majority but did not discuss a bill of rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not a Yugoslavist theme, though the idea contested the Habsburg borders that divided South Slavs.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Corfu pact specified a hereditary Karadjordjevic monarchy, not an elected ruler.

minority-veto.rationale: The pact set majority rules, with a qualified majority for the constitution, so a veto for a single dissenter is not envisaged.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Yugoslav nationalists resisted the Habsburgs, but the doctrine did not address resistance against its own monarch.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The pact described a parliamentary monarchy yet integral Yugoslavists sided with royal power, so the strands split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in Yugoslavist sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The duty of the privileged is not a topic in the doctrine, though ORJUNA criticised feudal privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Yugoslavism was an activist political nationalism in which committed adherents organised and fought for unification.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of media is absent from the doctrine.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is absent from the doctrine.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not part of the core doctrine, though Tito's Yugoslavia echoed Non-Aligned rhetoric.

native-born-offices.rationale: Yugoslav offices were meant for all South Slavs, but a nativity rule is not discussed.

party-own-road.rationale: Titoist Yugoslavia broke with Moscow in 1948 to follow its own road under brotherhood and unity.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The doctrine has no development theory; socialist Yugoslavia took Western aid, so it is not a stable position.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The pact's territorial claim for all South Slav lands and refusal to cede parts implies recovering them; weak inference.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not applicable to the Yugoslav case.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Brotherhood and Unity was coined in the wartime People's Liberation War against fascist occupation, and socialist Yugoslavia founded itself on it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Interwar Yugoslavists banned the Communists and opposed fascism, while Titoists rejected the equivalence; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical dispute irrelevant to the doctrine.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument politics is not covered by the doctrine, and socialist Yugoslavia pulled down monuments of the old regime.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Yugoslavists borrowed Western parliamentary forms and framed no civilisational case against them.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The interwar Yugoslav army and the monarch's generals served as guarantors of unity, and Tito's army was a pillar of the later state.

paid-care-work.rationale: The recognition of domestic labour is not a Yugoslavist demand.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duties are not set out in Yugoslavist sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not discussed in the doctrine.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign investment rules are not part of the doctrine.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not part of the doctrine, and religious communities would differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is a socialist-council idea that the doctrine does not share as such.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is outside the doctrine.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The doctrine contains no theory of community land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The pact provided for an elected national representative body in a parliamentary monarchy; budgetary power inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist Yugoslavism, after 1948, feared Soviet pressure but later moved to decentralise and promote self-management; the wider idea has no such doctrine.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Yugoslavists promoted a shared South Slav history from the Illyrian movement on, centring the Yugoslav nation in teaching; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism treated Serbs, Croats and Slovenes as one people with one "Serbo-Croato-Slovene" language, inferred from that one-nation premise; the Corfu pact gave both scripts equal standing.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The movement had no land-ownership programme; nothing in the sources addresses foreign buyers, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its civic-national and later class-based outlook: it held that peoples are equal in law and did not judge discrimination by group outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Yugoslavism was a national-unity idea with no stance on consumption; its liberal and socialist strands would split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: a newly founded, defensive South Slav state sought security through diplomacy and alliances rather than backing foreign rebels, though integral Yugoslavists made irredentist claims.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the Corfu pact, which framed unification as voluntary union of equals; brotherhood and unity stressed equal nations coexisting.

corporate-influence.rationale: Yugoslavism had no economic programme; its strands ranged from liberals to Communists, so the position is neutral.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerned unity of South Slavs rather than control of foreign funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred as neutral since its strands differ on social policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; integral Yugoslavism wanted one centralised nation, which weighs against local limits, but adherents are split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Strands ranged from liberal to Communist, so there is no settled position on state job guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from the Pact of Corfu's call for a constitutional, democratic and parliamentary state, but this is not tied to claims about peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; adherents ranged from liberals to authoritarian integralists, so neutral.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology was about South Slav unification and stressed national self-determination, so neutral.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; strands differ on economics.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism sought one nation from Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and rejected ethnic hostility within it, though ORJUNA-style groups were hostile to some outsiders; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the Corfu pact's reliance on established religions and family; not addressed directly.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Corfu Declaration promised a constitutional, parliamentary state but did not discuss access to information; neutral.

informal-organisation.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism was organised through parties and groups such as ORJUNA, and the Corfu pact envisaged a formal state; informal small-group organising is not part of it.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Corfu pact stressed a sovereign unified state; whether national law outranks international law is not addressed.

religious-nation.rationale: The Corfu Declaration unites Serbs, Croats and Slovenes of three faiths (Orthodox, Catholic, Muslim) on equal terms, so the nation is not defined by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Yugoslavism asserted a South Slav state equal to other states, and the idea of tribute is not addressed; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism favoured a centralised single state with pooled resources rather than regional retention; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Liberal, nationalist and socialist strands differed on property, so the answer is neutral and inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Yugoslavism was a unity idea with no stance on communism; its strands ranged from anti-communist to Titoist, inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No service-delivery policy belongs to the idea of South Slav unity; strands split on left-right lines.

religion-illusion.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism was anticlerical but the Corfu pact treated faiths equally, so adherents split; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Strands split on economics, so the answer is neutral and inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's equality was not part of the unity idea and strands split on economics; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: No domestic-work policy belongs to the idea; strands split on economics, inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Corfu pact assumed one nation with one language in two scripts, and mentions no purge of loanwords; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed by Yugoslavism; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Yugoslavism aimed at a single national state, not small cooperative communities; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism sought to merge the nation, and interwar policy encouraged Serb settlement in Kosovo and Macedonia; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Strands split on economics, so the answer is neutral and inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Yugoslavism rests on South Slav union rather than on one people's historical right to a land; inferred, since the Corfu pact treats the three peoples as equals on shared territory.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed in the period; inferred as a rejection from the movement's liberal-national, Entente-aligned outlook.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from interwar Balkan norms; the movement's sources never take up the question.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Corfu pact promised a parliamentary monarchy, but the integral strand backed the 1929 royal dictatorship and its ban on ethnic parties, so adherents split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Corfu pact makes all recognised religions equal before the law, which is incompatible with state punishment of false religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Yugoslavism concerns a union of kin peoples, not overseas rule; inferred as disagreement from its national-self-determination framing.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not a concern of the movement; inferred, as Yugoslavism was secular-national and counted Muslims as South Slavs.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Corfu pact grounds the state in a constitution and the people's will, not religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Corfu pact planned representative parliamentary government, while integral Yugoslavism stressed unity under the state; the socialist strand's self-management differs, so inferred as split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; the movement put national unity above social divisions, so inferred disagreement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the traditional social outlook of the interwar kingdom.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the period's religious and traditional norms in the South Slav lands.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism sought one supra-tribal nation above regional and party loyalties, which is close to a politics beyond old divisions; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation is a Marxist concept: the socialist strand (brotherhood and unity under Tito) would agree, the integral and monarchist strands would not.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Yugoslavism counted Bosnian Muslims among the Yugoslav nation and the Corfu pact guaranteed Muslim equality; inferred disagreement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Corfu pact derives the state from the nation and a constitution, not from God; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' secular unity ideal and equal recognised religions do not settle the question.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economics divided the strands (the Corfu pact is silent; socialist strand favoured planning), so inferred as split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Yugoslavism built a national army as a pillar of the new state; inferred strong disagreement with abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Both the integral and socialist strands stressed equality of the peoples and citizens; inferred disagreement.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The interwar kingdom allied with France and the Little Entente, while the socialist strand later led non-alignment, so adherents split by strand.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: the interwar Karadjordjevic kingdom, the Corfu pact's constitutional monarchy, was the vehicle of Yugoslavism, so hereditary succession was accepted; the socialist strand differed.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: no credit policy belongs to South Slav unity; strands ranged from liberal to Titoist.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: the idea says nothing on lenders; later Titoist Yugoslavia both borrowed from and resisted the West, so adherents split.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: the Corfu pact calls for universal, equal and secret suffrage, so a property franchise runs against it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: ecofeminist theory is unrelated to a national-unity idea, so there is no adherent position.

reification.rationale: Inferred: reification is a Marxist concept; only the socialist strand would engage with it, and the mainstream profile is silent.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: liberal and socialist Yugoslavists would split on this, and the idea itself does not address press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: the Corfu pact set out a constitutional, parliamentary monarchy under law, which implies rule by standing laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Corfu pact gives Serbs, Croats and Slovenes equal rights as one nation, and integral Yugoslavism merged them; a franchise limited to one ethnic group contradicts its core.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the internet postdates the idea; no adherent position can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic: open-data publication is a modern idea the movement never addressed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the Corfu pact gave Orthodox, Catholic and Muslim faiths equal rights, so legal limits on interfaith marriage conflict with it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: Yugoslavism sought unity among the South Slavs and equal religious standing, so religious boycotts cut against it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the interwar movement favoured a constituent assembly and a centralised parliamentary state, but sortition-based assemblies were not discussed and adherents ranged from liberals to Communists.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the Pact of Corfu made the three faiths equal and integral Yugoslavism was strongly anticlerical, which favours subordinating inherited religious authority to the unifying nation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Integral and federalist strands diverge on economics and the sources do not discuss wealth concentration, so it is genuinely split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by Yugoslavists; interwar and Titoist-era mainstream attitudes were socially conservative, so this is inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Corfu pact declared the recognised religions equal and free, which rules out a state campaign for atheism in the interwar mainstream, though the socialist strand differed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Yugoslavists sought a strong unified state whose order depended on police and courts; abolition is far from the project.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism denied that Serbs, Croats and Slovenes are separate communities needing shared power, treating them as one nation; federalists differed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not addressed; strands split on economics and no stated view on charity versus state aid exists.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; the monarchist unitary-state mainstream had no term-limit tradition, so this is inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegated voting is anachronistic; the mainstream wanted a representative constitutional state, so a negative answer is inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic to the movement; no basis for a stated position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; the mainstream's churches were male-led and the movement did not challenge this, inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Strands diverge: interwar society was patriarchal while the Titoist strand proclaimed equality; no stated common view.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; the Corfu pact tied rights to citizens of one nation-state, so this is inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Strands ranged from liberals to Communists and the sources do not address housing; adherents are split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's mainstream liberal and national-cultural strands, which supported creators' rights.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The integral Yugoslav movement ORJUNA was a paramilitary youth organisation, and Tito's era had a Pioneer and Youth Union system.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic for the interwar strand; later Titoist non-alignment leaned against it, so adherents are split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the stress on a sovereign united South Slav state; Titoist non-alignment later refused foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; Yugoslavism's brotherhood and unity line sought to avoid exposing wartime atrocities, while others favoured naming them.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The strands diverge; the socialist strand agrees, the liberal and integral strands do not.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nothing in the sources suggests pacifism; the integral strand was militant and the Titoist strand was a partisan movement.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Yugoslavism built a new composite nation out of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, rather than treating an ancient nation as continuous.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Mixed: the integral strand honoured national heroes and the Titoist strand honoured partisan fallen, but the sources do not address sacred martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Yugoslavism was secular and national-political; not addressed, inferred from that character.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The aim was to gather the South Slavs into one state, not to serve a diaspora; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Pact of Corfu demanded a common state first; although the Illyrian movement began with culture, the political programme put the state first.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Yugoslavism aimed to unite several peoples with equal standing, which cuts against reserving business for one group; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Yugoslavism aimed at joining South Slav lands into one state, and the integral strand wanted to centralise rather than divide; its federalist strand differed, so inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The idea was about national unity; its adherents ranged from liberals to Communists on this.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Adherents spanned liberal and Communist strands, so there is no common position.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No common economic programme; the strands differed.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; the strands differed on institutions.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the integral strand's centralism and the absence of a municipal-ownership programme.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism favoured a centralised single nation rather than confederation, though federalist strands differed.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the integral strand's priority of the national community over individuals.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed; adherents included both religious and secular people.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the integral strand's centralism, though the federalist strand would disagree.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the idea of a single South Slav nation whose parts should not organise as separate groups.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; the pride at issue was South Slav national pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed directly; the idea was about unification, and adherents' views on war varied.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Yugoslavism held that Serbs, Croats and Slovenes are one people by blood and language, despite different religions and state borders, as the Corfu pact states.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Corfu pact and integral Yugoslavism sought one nation with equal citizenship across Orthodox, Catholic and Muslim lines, so separate religious electorates cut against its aim.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Yugoslav unionists, and later the kingdom, saw Italian and other neighbours' ambitions as a threat to the South Slavs' unity; inferred from the integral Yugoslav defensive nationalism, not from a stated source claim.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy was not part of Yugoslavism; liberal unionists and socialist Titoists differed, so this is neutral.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation was not part of this national-unity idea, and strands differed; inferred neutral.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the nation-building aim of founding a lasting common state for future generations of South Slavs.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by Yugoslavism; its strands ranged from liberal to socialist and had no common view on gender.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not a stated position; the interwar kingdom built up its army, while Titoist Yugoslavia promoted non-aligned peace diplomacy, so adherents were split.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; the Corfu pact was itself negotiated by exiled politicians, and strands differed on diplomacy, so neutral.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic strands diverged, as the scope notes: liberals favoured open markets, Titoists favoured state control, so neutral.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not a stated theme; a unitary South Slav state would be expected to keep arms under state control; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Yugoslavism was a state-building nationalism that backed defence of the union; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Adherents ranged from liberals to Communists, so no line on bargaining can be given.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Economics divided the strands and the idea itself had no programme; inferred as split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Economics divided the strands and the idea itself had no programme; inferred as split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; strands diverge, from interwar monarchists to Tito's non-aligned socialists.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Mainstream Yugoslavism aimed to build one state, not smash it, though Communists differed; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Titoist self-management was an experiment but mainstream integral Yugoslavism had no economic blueprint; split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; the idea had no ecological programme.

sacred-nation.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism treated the South Slav nation as an organic, lasting unity worth political sacrifice.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split by wing on social spending.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism held the nation to be one, so claims of one part exploiting another contradict it, though Croats and Slovenes made them; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The idea rests on shared blood and kinship among South Slavs; a common nature for humans is inferred as an acceptable background.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between liberal and state-controlled views.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Corfu pact treated Orthodox, Catholic and Muslim faiths as equal and adherents ranged from believers to Communists, so they are split.

farm-price-support.rationale: No agrarian programme belongs to the idea; liberal and socialist Yugoslavists differed.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; no position follows from South Slav unity, and socialist Yugoslavia was non-aligned.

workers-own-party.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism was a cross-class national idea that sought one nation, so separate workers' parties were not its aim.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; modernising unitary-state liberals would back a ban. Inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Corfu pact promised equal rights and universal suffrage; equal property rights are inferred from this.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The Corfu pact calls the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes one nation of one language, and integral Yugoslavism treated their varieties as one language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; its adherents split along ordinary left-right lines.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the modernising, state-building aim of the Corfu pact, which sets up a parliamentary monarchy with a constituent assembly.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split along ordinary lines.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split along ordinary lines.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from integral Yugoslavism's drive for one common national language; not directly stated.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Yugoslavism was a national-unity idea with no labour programme; its strands ranged from liberal to socialist.

voter-id.rationale: The sources do not discuss voter identification; no position can be drawn.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Corfu pact declared the three faiths equal and equally free, which leaves no interpretation privileged.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Corfu pact planned a parliamentary constitutional monarchy, but integral Yugoslavism was authoritarian and the socialist strand ruled one-party; strands diverge.

premarital-sex.rationale: Interwar Yugoslavism was socially conservative in this respect; inferred from the era's norms, with the radical ORJUNA strand not settled.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed in the period; strands split between liberal and authoritarian outlooks.

negative-income-tax.rationale: No economic programme; strands differ on economics, as the scope notes.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Corfu pact promised universal, equal, direct and secret suffrage; women are not mentioned, so this is inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Integral Yugoslavism was anticlerical in part, but it did not centre women; inferred and weak.

race-social-construct.rationale: Yugoslavism claimed one nation by blood and language, which treats ethnic stock as natural, yet it did not use biological races; adherents differ.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed in the period; socialist strand later had women's bodies but the mainstream did not.

missingStatements.text: The South Slavs form a single nation that should live in one state.
missingStatements.rationale: The Corfu pact calls Serbs, Croats and Slovenes one nation of one blood and language and demands a single kingdom for them.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be able to use more than one alphabet or script in public life on an equal footing.
missingStatements.rationale: The Corfu pact gave Cyrillic and Latin equal standing and made authorities use both as citizens wished.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Corfu pact; the nearest statement, minority-language-support, is answered 0 here, so it does not capture this.

missingStatements.text: A state should treat several recognised religions as equal before the law without privileging one.
missingStatements.rationale: The Corfu pact gave Orthodox, Catholic and Muslim faiths equal rights, while interwar practice favoured the Serbian Orthodox Church.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Corfu pact and contradicted by interwar practice; the nearest statement, separate-church-state, is answered 0 here.

notes: Strands diverge: federalists (Radić, Supilo, Trumbić) against integralists (Pribićević, ORJUNA) on centralism, and socialist Yugoslavism on property and party rule. Most statements outside nation, state-form and religion are neutral because Yugoslavism was a cross-class national idea.
